refusal_fallback.comment: [R86 round 4, docs/REFUSAL-FALLBACK-2026-10-09.md] what the kernel does when the LLM declines a request (kernel/refusal.py judges every user-facing answer): "preamble" = the same model again with prompts.ADULT_PREAMBLE prepended to the system prompt (no model swap); "llm_uncensored" = the uncensored LLM: a tier's llm_uncensored section when it has one, else the default llm when that carries "uncensored": true (this tier: the heretic Gemma 4 IS the default since 2026-10-10 and, since R89, the only coder LLM, so the rung is skipped while the default answers; it serves a censored primary on a manifest that has one). The rung never runs the model that declined (compared by file); a section's file absent / empty / incomplete or a failed load skips it too. Every rung declined -> the request is DECLINED: a plain error for the user, nothing cached, nothing rendered, never a 502. expander_ladder = the image-prompt expander's own cheap rungs: "preamble" first (integrator 2026-10-09: 0/20 refused expansions with it, results/r86-refusal-fallback/screen/SCREEN.md), then "encoder" = the image section's baked text encoder (or its optional expander_fallback_file) with the krea-18plus rules; every rung refused -> the picture is declined, never rendered from the refusal or the raw prompt. The narrow minors block (refusal.minor_block, round 4b lists: an explicit under-18 age or word together with a sexual term; csam / pthc / child porn / kiddie porn / Kinderporno / jailbait on their own; loli / shota with a sexual term; never a negated or age-gate disclaimer, an age difference or a measurement) runs at every media entry, on the final image/video prompt, once on a refused text request before any rung, and at the entry when the primary LLM is uncensored; it cannot be configured away.

llm.role: HTML app generation + Python game generation
llm.name: Gemma 4 26B-A4B-it ultra-uncensored heretic (i1-IQ4_XS, MoE, experts partly in RAM)
llm.comment: [R86 round 4] The owner's choice (2026-10-10 21:35, the model triage page): the uncensored heretic edition (mradermacher's i1-IQ4_XS of the same gemma4 MoE architecture, 128 experts / 8 active) is the default LLM; stock Gemma 4 26B-A4B-it (unsloth UD-IQ4_XS, 13 597 177 568 B) left the manifests and the stick (it stays on the build host). Same serve args. "uncensored": true tells the kernel that this model answers adult requests itself: the refusal ladder's uncensored rung is this very model (skipped when it is the primary) and the narrow minors block (kernel/refusal.py minor_block) checks every text request at the entry. The measurements below were taken on stock Gemma (same architecture; the llm-ps benchmark on the heretic ran 2026-10-10, unit kairos-llmps-heretic). Feature test 2026-09-28 (docs/FEATURE-TEST-2026-09-28.md §6): 36/37 functional app items, text editor 6/6, 7/7 apps error-free at first load vs 11/37 for Qwen2.5-Coder-7B and 13/37 for Qwen3.5-9B — the only candidate whose generated apps work; LiveCodeBench 65 % / AIME 60 % (docs/LLM-PROBLEM-SOLVING-2026-09.md). Costs: 3–4.7 min per app (28.8 tok/s, prompt 535 tok/s), llama-server RSS 15.5 GB (mmap'd GGUF), 6.4–8.2 s reload after every image job. 13.6 GB MoE on the 8 GB card: NO -ngl here on purpose — llama.cpp b11223's `--fit` (default on) placed it in the benchmark (all 31 layers' dense weights on CUDA0, the MoE experts of ~22 of 31 layers overflow to system RAM, 6.7 GB VRAM). `--reasoning off` + enable_thinking=false as for Qwen3.5. Vendor sampling: temp 1.0, top_k 64, top_p 0.95. [R89] No separate fast model any more (the owner, 2026-10-18: "Drop fast mode"): the llm_fast add-on (Qwen2.5-Coder-7B, 40 s per app but 11/37 functional items vs 26–30/37 for this model, docs/FAST-MODELS-2026-10-17.md §1) left the 8 and 16 GB tiers; llm_model=fast serves this model.
llm.parallel_comment: 2 llama-server slots, each with the full -c above (-c 2*C -np 2 --no-kv-unified) [R72]: two LLM requests at once; CPU-measured 2026-10-06 (docs/PARALLEL-LLM-2026-10-06.md), GPU validation follows the current GPU benchmark

image.name: Muse (Krea 2 fine-tune by Stable Yogi, uncensored) — v3.5 Extended Q4_0
image.comment: v7.5-1 default [R76 → Muse, docs/IMAGE-MODEL-MUSE-2026-10-10.md]: Muse by Stable Yogi v3.5 Extended, a Krea 2 fine-tune by Stable_Yogi (civitai model 2741166, version 3258948 'v3.5 Q4 Extended'), the author's Q4_0 GGUF (256 Q4_0 + 174 F32 tensors, arch qwen_image, city96-style names — loads on the shipped sd.cpp 3f8527a like the Krea GGUFs). It replaces Krea 2 Turbo Q4_K_M + the Kroma v0.3 LoRA (both files leave the image: −1.14 GB net). Owner 2026-10-09: 'catch the krea2 model from the download folder embedd it instead of the uncencored krea you made'. GPU A/B 2026-10-10 on the RTX 4070 (vibeos-cuda-next/results/muse-2026-10-09/REPORT.md, 9 prompts, seed 42, 1024², shipped engine): 8 steps / CFG 1.0 chosen — median 51.6 s per sd-cli picture vs 67.6 s for the old default. The author: 8–20 steps, CFG 1–2.5 (never above 3), euler/simple, 1024–2048, the Qwen3-VL encoder + the Qwen-Image VAE (already baked), no trigger words. Expander krea-neutral (people exactly as requested, every person an adult 25+ whenever nudity or sex is involved; krea-18plus on an explicit adult request). `image_safe` = the same files with the SFW expander. Krea 2's official settings and the encoder/VAE facts: docs/IMAGE-MODELS-2026-09.md §7.
image.licence: Krea 2 community licence (base model) + civitai permissions of model 2741166 by Stable_Yogi: credit required (allowNoCredit false), no commercial use beyond RentCivit, no derivatives / relicensing — fine for the free, non-commercial kAIrOS; the file is redistributed unmodified

image_safe.comment: Muse with SFW prompts [R76 → Muse]: the same files as `image` (nothing to download, 0 bytes) rendered through the SFW expander (Krea's expansion.txt rule 8 'Assume clothing covers…' + the kAIrOS medium line). The stock, safety-tuned Krea 2 DiT left the image on 2026-10-10 (space: the stick keeps ≥ 2 GB free), so the safety of this choice now comes from the prompt rewrite alone — a decensored fine-tune renders what the expanded prompt asks for. Kept so the `safe` setting, /api/models and the Settings app keep working.

image_qwen.licence: Qwen Research License — research or evaluation purposes only; redistribution allowed (a downloadable add-on, never baked into the image)
image_qwen.comment: second image model [R42]: Alibaba Qwen-Image-2.1 (2026-09-14, 7B, best-ranked open model — LMArena 1228 / AA 1035), text rendering: poster, chalkboard, ß, 3-cat layout all correct in the 2026-09-28 A/B (docs/IMAGE-MODELS-2026-09.md §7). image_edit.name: Qwen-Image-2.1 Turbo edit (Q4_K_M, 8 steps) — the ✨ picture editor
image_edit.comment: [R85, docs/PICTURE-EDIT-2026-10-15.md] ✨ improve a picture: Muse (`image`) creates, this section edits a picture with the user's words — POST /api/image/improve, an sd-server session whose request carries the picture as its reference image (extra_images; sd-cli -r), `vision` = the Qwen3-VL-8B mmproj (--llm_vision). Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo (Qwen, 2026-10-09: the official 8-step distill of Qwen-Image-2.1, text-to-image AND edit, CFG 1) with its saved schedule: --sigmas = model_index.json sample_sigmas + the terminal 0, --steps 8 = sigmas - 1 (the shipped sd.cpp 3f8527a; no --scheduler, no --flow-shift); the user's image_steps/cfg/sampler/scheduler tuning never applies here. Chosen by the GPU A/B of 2026-10-15 on Muse pictures (10 SFW + 5 adult edits, RTX 4070 8 GB, the shipped engine): vs Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 Q3_K_M + Lightning 4-step (20 GB, Apache) the same warm speed (66.5 vs 67.9 s per 1024² edit), first edit 82.5 vs 109.3 s, peak RSS 8.1 vs 20.4 GB (fits next to the 13.9 GB heretic on 31 GB), 0.004 vs 0.114 change outside the edited region, text written exactly; by eye 14/15 each, 18+ never re-censored (5/5). VRAM peak 7.3 GB. session_idle_s: R79's idle window for this section (a second ✨ within 2 minutes joins the open session; any other GPU waiter still closes it at once). An add-on: the v7.5-2 media image pre-installs it; elsewhere vibe.models.download('image_edit'). The VAE is the image_qwen add-on's (one file).
image_edit.licence: Qwen Research License (Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo + its VAE, Alibaba / Tongyi Lab): use for non-commercial (research or evaluation) purposes; redistribution as part of a product allowed with a copy of the licence and the NOTICE (§3) — fine for the free, non-commercial kAIrOS. The Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct encoder GGUF + mmproj: Apache-2.0.

video.name: Wan2.2-TI2V-5B (Q4_K_M)
video.comment: Wan2.2-TI2V-5B — downloadable add-on. 33 frames (= 9 latent frames): with 17 the DiT collapsed into a colour mosaic on 5 of 8 seeds whatever the cfg/shift/steps/negative prompt, with 33 all 8 seeds converge (docs/ENGINES-CUDA-2026-09.md 9.2). The VAE decodes on the GPU in 128x128-PIXEL tiles = the same 8x8-latent tiles as before: sd.cpp master-929 reads --vae-tile-size in image pixels (minimum 64) — the old `8x8` was the latent-unit spelling of the 2026-09-14 engine and fails on this engine with 'VAE tile size must be at least 64 image pixels' (docs/FEATURE-TEST-2026-09-28.md D10). Verified 2026-09-28 on the RTX 4070: 33 frames in 102.7 s, 5.5 GB peak (the 256 px default: 98.7 s, 5.7 GB). Tiling stays: the old engine's default tile needed 13 GB and --vae-on-cpu spent 368 of a 402 s job on the RTX 4070 and 347 of 514 s on the 780M — same flags are the fast ones on CUDA and Vulkan/UMA. Boot animation falls back to the baked default clip when this is not installed.

music.name: ACE-Step 1.5 turbo (Q8, acestep.cpp)
music.comment: downloadable add-on [R47]; needs the acestep.cpp engine (scripts/install-engines.sh builds ace-lm/ace-synth). Two-stage pipeline, request-JSON driven (acestep.cpp docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): cmd[0] ace-lm turns request.json into request0.json (metadata + lyrics + audio codes), cmd[1] ace-synth renders request0.json to request00.wav next to it. The kernel writes 'request' + caption/lyrics/duration/seed as the JSON; model names are exact GGUF filenames in {models}/music. turbo DiT = 8 steps (base/sft = 50). cmd[1] decodes the VAE in 512-frame tiles (--vae-chunk 512 --vae-overlap 64, docs/MUSIC-FIXES-2026-10-23.md): the engine default 1024 OOMs on 8 GB at 40 s and from 120 s up, 512/64 holds a flat 4.3 GB up to 512 s.

vision.name: Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct (Q4_K_M + Q8_0 mmproj, llama-server)
vision.comment: downloadable add-on [R70]: the image model's LLM text encoder (image.text_encoder, Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct-GGUF Q4_K_M, Apache-2.0, on disk in every tier — the same file the prompt expander runs under llama-server, docs/INTEGRATION-2026-09-28.md) IS a vision-language model — with its mmproj projector the already-built llama-server runs it (llama.cpp docs/multimodal.md: -m <weights> --mmproj <projector>; images go to /v1/chat/completions as OpenAI image_url content parts). Only the 454 MB projector is downloaded: 'weights' references the image model's file, never a copy. --image-max-tokens caps what one picture costs in the 8k context (the kernel also fits it to 1280 px).

translation.name: Index-Translate 2B Q4_K_M on the CPU (fast) + the loaded LLM (quality)
translation.comment: downloadable add-on [R71]: the translation layer's MT model (docs/TRANSLATION-LAYER-2026-10-06.md; research docs/TRANSLATION-2026-10-06.md). `fast` = Bilibili IndexTeam Index-Translate-2B (2026-09-30, Apache-2.0, 150 languages, qwen35 architecture; self-reported WMT24++ 0.849) on its OWN llama-server on the CPU (-ngl 0 -dev none, port 8085, 4 slots): a UI-string batch never evicts the coder LLM or an image job under strategy swap — still the provisional fast choice of the CPU benchmark (docs/TRANSLATION-BENCH-2026-10-07.md). `quality` [R89, the owner 2026-10-18: "Translation via Gemma"] = the loaded LLM itself ({"use": "llm"}): the GPU benchmark (docs/FAST-MODELS-2026-10-17.md §2) measured the heretic Gemma at COMET-22 0.8684 vs 0.8710 (Hy-MT2-7B) and 0.8706 (Index-Translate-9B Q4_K_M, this tier's quality file until R89, 5.78 GB) — inside the 0.005 rule — with a 2.9–3.0 s cycle (a translation + the next Gemma answer) vs 11.9–12.6 s with the swap to a dedicated model; so no quality file, no download, no swap, no translation server for quality. Prompt per the model card for both: one user message, no system message, temperature 0 (`sampling` below — the LLM's own vendor sampling is left out), thinking off (chat_template_kwargs; the kernel also strips <think>). Settings: translation off|on (default off = nothing runs), language en|de|es|fr|it|ja|ru, translation_quality fast|quality. vibe.models.download('translation') fetches the fast file (built into the image anyway, `bake`); sha256/size_bytes from the Hugging Face API 2026-10-06. --cache-ram 0 on the fast server [P3 fix 3, 2026-10-07]: llama-server's server-side prompt cache defaults to 8192 MiB and grew the fast server from 1.9 to 10.95 GB RSS over ~1 800 requests (docs/TRANSLATION-BENCH-2026-10-07.md); translation requests are single-shot, the kernel's own cache answers repeats.

quality.comment: [R89] quality translation = the loaded LLM (the one serving the coder role, llm_choice — the heretic Gemma 4 here): TRANSLATE_PROMPT as one user message, no system prompt, temperature 0, thinking off, the same max_tokens min(2048, 64 + 3·len) — the body that scored COMET-22 0.8684; one such request at a time, so an app generation keeps the LLM's other slot. No file, no download, no swap. The 16 GB tier and up keep their dedicated 9B (not measured on a 16 GB card).

dictionaries.name: Dictionaries: BEOLINGUS de-en + 37 FreeDict pairs among en/de/es/fr/it/ja/ru
dictionaries.comment: downloadable add-on [R71 P3, 2026-10-07]: word lookup for GET /api/dict?word=&from=&to= / vibe.dict(word, from?, to?) (docs/TRANSLATION-LAYER-2026-10-06.md 'P3 + fixes'; research docs/TRANSLATION-2026-10-06.md §3). Works with the translation setting off. The kernel (kernel/dictionary.py) builds a compact folded index per dictionary and direction under cache/dict on first use or right after the download and binary-searches it through mmap (nothing loaded into RAM). BEOLINGUS (TU Chemnitz Ding de-en.txt.gz, ~205k lines, indexed in both directions) first for de<->en, then the FreeDict dictd archives; a direction without a forward file (it->fr, ja->it, ru->ja) is served by the reverse of the opposite pair; es<->ja has no dictionary. Licences (each archive carries its COPYING): BEOLINGUS GPL-2+; FreeDict deu-eng/eng-deu 1.9-fd1 = the Ding data under GPL-3+/AGPL-3+; the 2025.11.23 pairs = WikDict, CC-BY-SA 3.0; jpn-deu/jpn-eng/jpn-fra/jpn-rus = JMdict, CC-BY-SA 3.0; deu-ita/ita-deu 0.2.1, eng-fra 0.1.6, fra-eng 0.4.1, spa-eng 0.3.1, spa-deu 0.1 = GPL-2+. Checksums: sha512 = FreeDict's published sums (pod/translation-2026-10-06.queue), sha256 computed 2026-10-07 from the sha512-verified downloads (the kernel verifies both); BEOLINGUS sha256 from the queue. 118 MB in all.
